title: Resume browser — the Projects, Tags and Most recent chips and their menus

steps.path: Open a past conversation → the row of chips under the search box
steps.headline: The three chips are now the same size and shape as every other filter chip in the app, with a real chevron.
steps.changed: Chip text went from 11 px to 14 px, the tiny grey triangle became the chevron the app's dropdown fields use, and it turns to point up while a menu is open.
steps.measured: 11 px → 14 px text; 9 px triangle → 12 px chevron
steps.notice: The row reads at a glance, and a chip with a filter applied is solid, the way a lit category chip in the Marketplace is.
steps.risk: A lit chip is bolder than the old faint tint, so a filtered list is harder to miss. That was the aim, but it is a stronger look.

steps.path: Open a past conversation → the search box
steps.headline: The search box is the same rounded search pill the Projects screen and the Marketplace use.
steps.changed: It was its own squarer box with a dimmer outline. Now it is the shared search pill, so it matches the chips directly under it.
steps.notice: Search and the chips read as one group instead of two different kinds of box.
steps.risk: The pill is a little shorter than the old box, so the list starts a few pixels higher.

steps.headline: The Projects menu has square check boxes, a count on each row, and a Clear button pinned at the bottom.
steps.changed: Rows are 28 px tall with the app's own check box, which stays square on rounded themes instead of turning into a circle. Counts only include what the list can show, so a project's number matches the rows you get. The uppercase CLEAR header moved to the bottom as a footer button that closes the menu and dims when nothing is picked.
steps.notice: Ticks look like ticks, the count sits at the right edge, and with many projects the list scrolls while Clear stays in place.

steps.headline: The Tags menu opens straight onto your tags, with Clear and Manage tags… together at the bottom.
steps.changed: Manage tags… moved from an uppercase header row to a footer beside a new Clear button, which is where every other menu in the app keeps its Manage… entry. Each tag row shows how many conversations carry it, like the project rows.
steps.notice: The first thing under the chip is a tag you can tick, not a settings link.

steps.path: Chips row → pick one tag or one project
steps.headline: A chip names the one thing you picked, and shows a count when you pick more.
steps.changed: One tag picked reads as that tag's name instead of '1 tag'; two or more read as 'Tags 2'. Projects does the same, and the old comma-joined list of two or three project names is gone.
steps.notice: Chips stay short enough for a phone, and you can see what the one filter is without opening the menu.
steps.risk: Two or three chosen projects no longer show their names on the chip; open the menu to see which ones.

steps.headline: The sort chip uses a drawn arrow that turns over, and lights up when the order is not newest-first.
steps.changed: The ↓ and ↑ characters inside the label became a drawn arrow like the app's other icons; it points down for newest first and turns up for oldest first.
steps.notice: One tap flips the order, the arrow turns, and the chip lights so you can tell the list is not in its usual order.
steps.risk: The lit chip is the strongest thing on the row while the order is flipped.

steps.path: On a phone-width window → chips row
steps.headline: On a phone the chips keep to one line and slide sideways instead of squashing Most recent onto two lines.
steps.changed: The row scrolls sideways when the chips do not fit, the way the quick chips above the message box do, with a soft fade at the edge that has more; no chip ever wraps its own label.
steps.notice: Every chip stays a single readable pill at 390 px wide.
steps.risk: The third chip can be partly off the right edge on a narrow phone until you slide the row; the fade is the only hint.

steps.headline: Should the sort chip open a small menu like Projects and Tags do, or stay a one-tap flip?
steps.today: The third chip flips the order with one tap and shows an arrow. The two beside it open menus and show a chevron.
steps.problem: Three chips in a row, two behaviours: the arrow chip opens nothing, which can surprise on the first tap.
steps.proposal: Keep the one-tap flip shown on this deck, or make the chip a menu with two rows, Most recent and Oldest first, so all three chips behave the same way.

options.label: One-tap flip
pros: The arrow shows the current order at a glance
cons: One chip behaves differently from its two neighbours

options.label: Two-row menu
pros: All three chips open a list, so the gesture is the same everywhere
Room to add other orders later, such as by name
cons: Two taps to flip the order
A two-row menu for what is really a yes-or-no choice

steps.headline: Should this screen say conversations instead of sessions, to match the chat?
steps.today: The chat calls them conversations ("Continue this conversation in a new tab"). This screen says Resume Session, Search sessions, No matching sessions, and its reopen button is also Resume Session.
steps.problem: A beta tester read two words for one thing and took the reopen button for the title repeated.
steps.proposal: Rename the copy on this screen only: title Past conversations, search box Search conversations, empty state No conversations match, reopen button Continue. Nothing else changes.

options.label: Say conversations
pros: One word for one thing across the app
The reopen button stops reading like the title
cons: Session still appears in the top bar and status bar until those are renamed too

options.label: Keep sessions
pros: Nothing to relearn for anyone used to it
cons: The chat and this screen keep using different words

steps.path: Pick a project or tag and watch the dialog
steps.headline: Should the past-conversations dialog keep one height so it stops jumping when a filter shrinks the list?
steps.today: The dialog is as tall as its list, up to a limit, and sits centred. Picking a filter that leaves one row shrinks it and re-centres it, so it drops about 120 px on screen.
steps.problem: The beta tester's single most confusing moment: the row they had just clicked slid away from under the pointer. The open menu now follows, so nothing is mis-clicked any more, but the lurch remains.
steps.proposal: Give the dialog a fixed height whenever there is room, so the frame stays put and only the rows inside change. With very few conversations the lower part of the dialog is empty space.

options.label: One steady height
pros: Nothing moves when you filter or type in the search
Chips and menus stay exactly where you clicked
cons: A short list leaves empty space at the bottom of the dialog

options.label: Keep it shrinking
pros: A short list gets a compact dialog
cons: The dialog keeps re-centring as you filter
